The returned count equals the length of s multiplied by the length of s plus one, divided by two (integer division), which corresponds to the well-known formula for the number of non-empty substrings of a string of a given length, since for a string of length n there are n choices for the starting index and for each starting index i there are n minus i choices for the ending index, summing to n*(n+1)/2 in total.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_240
nl_requirement: Given two sequences of integers, first and second, where first must be non-empty, the method returns a new sequence formed by removing the last element of first and appending all elements of second in their original order. The resulting sequence has a length equal to the length of first minus one plus the length of second, and its elements consist of the first (|first| - 1) elements of first followed by all elements of second.
translated_ensures: forall i :: 0 <= i < |second| ==> result[|first| - 1 + i] == second[i]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_242
nl_requirement: Given a string s, the method returns an integer count equal to the number of characters in s. The input string may be empty or contain any number of characters, and the returned count will always be a non-negative integer exactly equal to the length of s.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_257
nl_requirement: Given two integers a and b, the method returns a sequence of exactly two integers where the first element is b and the second element is a. The inputs may be any integer values with no restrictions.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_261
nl_requirement: The method takes two integer sequences a and b of the same length, where every element of b is non-zero. It returns a sequence of integers whose length equals the length of a, where each element at index k is the integer (truncated) quotient of a[k] divided by b[k].
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < |a| ==> result[k] == a[k] / b[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_262
nl_requirement: The method takes an integer array `arr` and an integer index `L`, where `L` must be between 0 and the length of `arr` inclusive. It returns two sequences: `firstPart` contains exactly the elements of `arr` from index 0 up to (but not including) index `L`, and `secondPart` contains exactly the elements of `arr` from index `L` to the end of the array. Together, the two returned sequences form a partition of the original array such that concatenating `firstPart` followed by `secondPart` yields the full contents of `arr` in their original order.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_264
nl_requirement: The method takes a single integer representing an age in human years and returns an integer representing the equivalent age in dog years. The returned value must equal exactly seven times the input value.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_266
nl_requirement: The method takes a single integer input representing the size (edge length) of a cube, and returns an integer representing the lateral surface area of that cube. The returned value must equal four times the square of the input size. The input size should be a non-negative integer to produce a meaningful geometric result.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_267
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer n, the method computes and returns the sum of the squares of the first n odd numbers (i.e., 1² + 3² + 5² + … + (2n−1)²). The returned value equals n × (2n − 1) × (2n + 1) / 3. If n is 0, the returned sum is 0.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_268
nl_requirement: Given an integer n, the method returns the nth star number, which is computed as 6 times n times (n minus 1), plus 1. The input n must be a non-negative integer. The returned value is exactly 6*n*(n-1)+1, which for n=0 gives 1, for n=1 gives 1, for n=2 gives 13, and so on, following the sequence of centered star polygonal numbers.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_269
nl_requirement: Given a single character c, the method returns its corresponding ASCII (integer) value. The returned integer is exactly the numeric code point of the input character c, obtained by a direct cast of the character to its underlying integer representation. There are no preconditions on the input character.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_273
nl_requirement: The method takes two integer sequences a and b of the same length as inputs, and returns a sequence result of the same length where each element at index k is the difference of the corresponding elements a[k] minus b[k]. Both input sequences must have equal length, and the returned sequence has exactly that same length with every position computed as the element-wise subtraction of b from a.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < |a| ==> result[k] == a[k] - b[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_276
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative real number radius and a non-negative real number height representing the dimensions of a cylinder, the method returns the volume of that cylinder computed as π times the square of the radius times the height, where π is approximated as 3.14159265359. The returned volume is therefore equal to 3.14159265359 multiplied by radius multiplied by radius multiplied by height.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_279
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer n, the method returns the nth decagonal number, which is computed as 4 times n squared minus 3 times n. The input n must be a non-negative integer, and the returned value must exactly equal 4 * n * n - 3 * n.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_282
nl_requirement: Both input arrays a and b must have the same length. The method returns a new integer array whose length equals the length of a, where every element at index i equals a[i] minus b[i] for all valid indices i.
translated_ensures: forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> result[i] == a[i] - b[i]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_284
nl_requirement: The method takes an integer array and an integer value n, and returns a boolean indicating whether every element in the array equals n. The result is true if and only if all elements in the array are equal to n; if any element differs from n, the result is false. There are no preconditions on the inputs beyond the array being a valid (non-null) array.
translated_ensures: result <==> forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> a[i] == n

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_292
nl_requirement: Given two integers a and b, where b must not be zero, the method returns the integer quotient of dividing a by b, using truncation toward zero for the division. The input b must be non-zero to ensure the division is well-defined.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_304
nl_requirement: Given a non-empty sequence of integers `l`, an integer `n` representing a rotation amount, and a valid index into the rotated sequence, the method returns the element that appears at position `index` in the sequence after it has been rotated to the right by `n` positions. The input sequence must be non-empty, and `index` must be a valid index into it (i.e., between 0 inclusive and the length of `l` exclusive). The rotation amount `n` may be any integer, and the method correctly handles negative values or values larger than the sequence length by using modular arithmetic. The returned element is the element from the original sequence `l` that, after shifting all elements `n` positions to the right (wrapping around), ends up at position `index`.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_307
nl_requirement: Given a sequence of integers s, the method returns a new sequence copy that has exactly the same length as s and whose elements are identical to those of s at every index — that is, for every valid index k, copy[k] equals s[k]. The input sequence s may be empty, in which case copy is also empty. There are no preconditions on s beyond it being a valid sequence of integers.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_309
nl_requirement: Given two integers a and b, the method returns an integer maxValue that is equal to whichever of a or b is greater. Specifically, maxValue must be greater than or equal to both a and b, and it must equal either a or b. There are no preconditions on the inputs; any integer values are acceptable.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_312
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative real number radius and a non-negative real number height, the method returns the volume of a cone with those dimensions, computed as one-third of pi (approximated as 3.14159265358979323846) multiplied by the square of the radius and then multiplied by the height.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_397
nl_requirement: Given three integer inputs a, b, and c, the method returns the median value among the three, meaning the returned value is one of the three inputs and is neither strictly greater than all others nor strictly less than all others. Specifically, the returned value m satisfies the property that the minimum of the three inputs is at most m and m is at most the maximum of the three inputs. There are no preconditions on the inputs; they may be any integers, including duplicates.
translated_ensures: median == a || median == b || median == c
median >= a || median >= b || median >= c
median <= a || median <= b || median <= c
(a <= median || b <= median || c <= median) && (a >= median || b >= median || c >= median)

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_404
nl_requirement: Given two integers a and b, the method returns the minimum of the two values. The returned value must be equal to a if a is less than or equal to b, and equal to b otherwise. In all cases, the returned value is less than or equal to both a and b, and is equal to at least one of them. There are no restrictions on the input values.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_430
nl_requirement: Given a parabola in vertex form with vertical axis of symmetry, where `a` is the leading coefficient (which must be non-zero), `h` is the x-coordinate of the vertex, and `k` is the y-coordinate of the vertex, the method returns the y-value of the directrix, which is the horizontal line located at k minus 1 divided by (4 times a). The input `a` must not be zero, as it appears in the denominator. The returned directrix value is independent of `h` and is uniquely determined by `k` and `a`.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_431
nl_requirement: Given two arrays of integers a and b, the method returns true if and only if there exists at least one integer value that appears in both a and b (i.e., there exist indices i and j such that a[i] equals b[j]); otherwise it returns false. Both arrays may be of any length, including zero, and no preconditions are placed on their contents.
translated_ensures: result <==> exists i, j :: 0 <= i < a.Length && 0 <= j < b.Length && a[i] == b[j]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_432
nl_requirement: Given two integer inputs a and b, the method returns the integer median, which is the floor of the arithmetic mean of a and b, computed as the integer division of their sum by 2. There are no preconditions on the inputs; any two integers are valid. The returned value is the truncated (floored toward zero) average of a and b, consistent with Dafny's built-in integer division semantics.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_433
nl_requirement: Given an integer n and an array a of integers, the method returns true if and only if n is strictly greater than every element in a. If a is empty, the result is true. If any element in a is greater than or equal to n, the result is false. The array a must be a valid (non-null) array, but there are no constraints on the values of n or the elements of a.
translated_ensures: result <==> forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> n > a[i]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_435
nl_requirement: Given an integer n, the method returns the last decimal digit of n, defined as the remainder when n is divided by 10. The returned value d satisfies d = n mod 10, consistent with Dafny's modulo semantics for integers.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_441
nl_requirement: The method takes a single integer input representing the side length of a cube, and returns an integer representing the total surface area of that cube. The returned value must equal six times the square of the input size, reflecting the fact that a cube has six square faces each with area equal to the side length squared.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_445
nl_requirement: The method takes two integer sequences a and b of the same length as inputs and returns a sequence result of the same length where each element at position k is the product of the corresponding elements a[k] and b[k]. The input sequences must have equal length, and the returned sequence has exactly that many elements, with every position satisfying result[k] == a[k] * b[k].
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < |a| ==> result[k] == a[k] * b[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_447
nl_requirement: Given a non-null integer array `a`, the method returns a new array `cubed` of the same length as `a` where every element at each index is the cube (third power) of the corresponding element in `a`; that is, for every valid index `k`, `cubed[k]` equals `a[k]` multiplied by itself three times.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < a.Length ==> cubed[k] == a[k] * a[k] * a[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_452
nl_requirement: Given a cost price and a selling price as integers, the method returns the loss as a non-negative integer. If the cost price is strictly greater than the selling price, the returned loss equals the difference between the cost price and the selling price (i.e., costPrice minus sellingPrice). Otherwise, when the selling price is greater than or equal to the cost price, the returned loss is zero, indicating no loss occurred.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_458
nl_requirement: Given two integer inputs, length and width, the method returns an integer area equal to their product, that is, length multiplied by width. There are no preconditions on the inputs; any integer values, including negative numbers and zero, are accepted.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_470
nl_requirement: The input array must contain at least zero elements (no precondition beyond being a valid array). The method returns a new array whose length is exactly the floor of half the input array's length. Each element at index k in the result is the sum of the two consecutive elements at positions 2*k and 2*k+1 in the input array, for every valid index k from 0 up to (but not including) the result's length. In other words, the input array is treated as a sequence of consecutive pairs, and each pair is collapsed into a single sum in the output.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < result.Length ==> result[k] == a[2*k] + a[2*k+1]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_474
nl_requirement: The method takes a string s, a character oldChar, and a character newChar, and returns a string v of the same length as s where every character that was equal to oldChar in s is replaced by newChar, and every character that was not equal to oldChar is left unchanged at the same position.
translated_ensures: forall i :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> (s[i] == oldChar ==> v[i] == newChar)
forall i :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> (s[i] != oldChar ==> v[i] == s[i])

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_555
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer n, the method computes and returns the difference between the sum of cubes of all integers from 1 to n (inclusive) and the sum of those same integers. Specifically, the returned value diff equals (n*(n+1)/2)^2 minus n*(n+1)/2, which is the sum of cubes 1^3 + 2^3 + ... + n^3 minus the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n. The input n must be a non-negative integer so that the iteration range is well-defined.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_572
nl_requirement: Given an array of integers, the method returns a sequence containing exactly the distinct values that appear in the array: every integer that appears at least once in the array is present in the result, every integer in the result appears somewhere in the array, and no integer appears more than once in the result. The input array may be empty, in which case the result is an empty sequence. There are no other preconditions on the input.
translated_ensures: forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> exists j :: 0 <= j < a.Length && a[j] == result[i]
forall j :: 0 <= j < a.Length ==> exists i :: 0 <= i < |result| && result[i] == a[j]
forall i, k :: 0 <= i < |result| && 0 <= k < |result| && i != k ==> result[i] != result[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_574
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative real number radius and a non-negative real number height representing the dimensions of a cylinder, the method returns the total surface area of that cylinder, computed as 2π times the radius times the sum of the radius and the height, where π is approximated as 3.14159265358979323846. The returned area is therefore equal to 2 × 3.14159265358979323846 × radius × (radius + height).

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_578
nl_requirement: The three input sequences must all have the same length. The returned sequence has length exactly three times the length of any input sequence, and consists of the elements of the three sequences interleaved element by element: for every valid index i, the element at position 3*i is s1[i], the element at position 3*i+1 is s2[i], and the element at position 3*i+2 is s3[i].

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_581
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer baseEdge representing the side length of a square base and a non-negative integer height representing the slant height of the triangular faces, the method returns the total surface area of a square pyramid computed as the area of the square base plus the combined area of the four triangular faces. Specifically, the returned area equals baseEdge multiplied by baseEdge (the base area) plus two times baseEdge times height (the lateral surface area), where both inputs are assumed to be non-negative integers.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_586
nl_requirement: The method takes a sequence of integers l and an integer n, where n must be a valid split point satisfying 0 <= n <= |l|. It returns a new sequence r that is a rotation of l: the elements from index n to the end of l come first, followed by the elements from the beginning of l up to (but not including) index n. The returned sequence r has the same length as l and contains exactly the same elements, just rearranged so that the suffix starting at position n becomes the prefix of r and the original prefix becomes the suffix.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_587
nl_requirement: Given an array of integers, the method returns a sequence of integers of the same length as the array, where every element in the returned sequence at each index equals the corresponding element in the input array at that same index.
translated_ensures: forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> s[i] == a[i]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_59
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer n, the method returns the nth octagonal number, which is computed as n multiplied by the quantity (3 times n minus 2). The input n must be a non-negative integer, and the returned value will equal n * (3 * n - 2).

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_599
nl_requirement: The input n must be a positive integer. The method returns two values: sum, which is the total of all integers from 1 through n inclusive (i.e., n multiplied by n plus one, divided by two), and average, which is that sum divided by n expressed as a real number.
translated_ensures: average == sum as real / n as real

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_602
nl_requirement: The method takes a string s and searches for the first character that appears more than once, where 'first' is determined by the earlier occurrence's position. It returns a boolean found and a character c. If found is true, then c is the character at some index ii in s such that c also appears at some later index jj (ii < jj), and no pair of equal characters (k, l) with k < l exists where l is strictly less than jj — meaning c is the repeated character whose second occurrence comes before the second occurrence of any other repeated character. If found is false, then no character in s appears more than once (all characters are distinct). The method has no preconditions on the input string, and when found is false the value of c is unspecified.
translated_ensures: found ==> exists ii :: 0 <= ii < |s| && s[ii] == c && exists jj :: ii < jj < |s| && s[jj] == c
found ==> exists ii, jj :: 0 <= ii < jj < |s| && s[ii] == c && s[jj] == c && forall k, l :: 0 <= k < l < |s| && s[k] == s[l] ==> jj <= l
!found ==> forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < |s| ==> s[i] != s[j]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_603
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer n, the method returns a sequence of integers containing exactly the multiples of 3 that lie in the range 0 to n (inclusive). Every element in the returned sequence must be divisible by 3, every element must be at most n, and the sequence must be strictly increasing (i.e., each element is greater than the one before it). The input n must be a non-negative integer.
translated_ensures: forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < |lucid| ==> lucid[i] < lucid[j]
forall k :: 0 <= k <= n && k % 3 == 0 ==> k in lucid

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_610
nl_requirement: Given an array s of integers and an index k, where k must be a valid index into s (i.e., 0 <= k < s.Length) and s must have at least one element, the method returns a new array v of length s.Length - 1 that contains all elements of s except the one at position k. Specifically, for every index j less than k, v[j] equals s[j], and for every index j from k to v.Length - 1, v[j] equals s[j + 1]. In other words, the returned array is s with the element at position k removed and all remaining elements preserving their relative order.
translated_ensures: forall j :: 0 <= j < k ==> v[j] == s[j]
forall j :: k <= j < v.Length ==> v[j] == s[j + 1]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_616
nl_requirement: The method takes two integer arrays a and b as input, where b must have at least as many elements as a and every element of b that corresponds to an index in a must be non-zero (to avoid division by zero in the modulo operation). It returns a new integer array whose length equals the length of a, where each element at index k contains the remainder of dividing a[k] by b[k], for all valid indices k from 0 up to but not including the length of a.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < a.Length ==> result[k] == a[k] % b[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_618
nl_requirement: The method takes two integer sequences a and b of the same length, where every element of b must be non-zero. It returns a sequence of integers with the same length as the inputs, where each element at index k equals a[k] divided by b[k] using integer division.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < |a| ==> result[k] == a[k] / b[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_62
nl_requirement: The input array must be non-empty. The method returns an integer that is the minimum value of the array: the returned value must be less than or equal to every element in the array, and it must actually appear as an element somewhere in the array.
translated_ensures: forall i :: 0 <= i < s.Length ==> min <= s[i]
exists i :: 0 <= i < s.Length && min == s[i]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_622
nl_requirement: Given two non-null integer arrays a and b, where a is non-empty and, if a has an even length, b must also be non-empty (so that b[0] is accessible), the method returns an integer median computed as follows: if the length of a is even, the result is the integer division of the sum of a[a.Length/2 - 1] and b[0] divided by 2; if the length of a is odd, the result is simply the middle element a[a.Length/2].

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_626
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer radius representing the radius of a semicircle, the method returns the area of the largest triangle that can be inscribed in that semicircle. The largest such triangle has its base equal to the diameter of the semicircle and its height equal to the radius, so the area equals radius multiplied by radius (i.e., the square of the radius). The input radius must be non-negative, and the returned area is always the square of the given radius.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_627
nl_requirement: Given a sequence of integers s, the method returns the smallest non-negative integer v that does not appear in s. The returned value v is guaranteed to be non-negative. Every non-negative integer strictly less than v must appear somewhere in s, and v itself must not appear in s. The method assumes that s is sorted in non-decreasing order for the result to be meaningful; specifically, the logic relies on elements being encountered in order so that the scan can stop early when an element exceeds the current candidate.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < v ==> k in s
translated_requires: forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < |s| ==> s[i] <= s[j]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_641
nl_requirement: Given a non-negative integer n, the method returns the nth nonagonal (9-gonal) number, computed as n multiplied by the quantity (7 times n minus 5), divided by 2. The input n must be a non-negative integer such that the expression n * (7 * n - 5) is even (i.e., divisible by 2) to ensure an integer result, and the returned value equals exactly n * (7 * n - 5) / 2.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_728
nl_requirement: The method takes two integer sequences a and b of the same length as inputs, and returns a sequence result of the same length where each element at index k is the sum of the corresponding elements a[k] and b[k]. Both input sequences must be non-null and have equal length.
translated_ensures: forall k :: 0 <= k < |a| ==> result[k] == a[k] + b[k]

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_733
nl_requirement: The array must be non-null. The method searches a sorted (non-decreasing) integer array for the first occurrence of the given target value and returns its index. If the target is found, the returned index is a valid position in the array (between 0 inclusive and the array length exclusive), the element at that index equals the target, and no element at any earlier index equals the target. If the target is not present in the array, the method returns -1. The array contents are not modified by this method.
translated_ensures: index == -1 || (0 <= index < arr.Length && arr[index] == target && forall k :: 0 <= k < index ==> arr[k] != target)
index == -1 ==> forall k :: 0 <= k < arr.Length ==> arr[k] != target

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_743
nl_requirement: The method takes a sequence of integers l and an integer n, and returns a sequence r of the same length as l where each element r[k] is equal to l[(k - n + |l|) % |l|], effectively rotating the sequence to the right by n positions so that the element originally at position (k - n + |l|) % |l| in l appears at position k in the result. The input sequence l must be non-empty (so that the modular index arithmetic is well-defined).

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_751
nl_requirement: Given an array of integers, the method returns true if and only if the array satisfies the min-heap property: for every index k in the range 0 to (length/2 - 1) inclusive, the element at index k is less than or equal to its left child at index 2k+1, and if a right child exists (i.e., index 2k+2 is within bounds), the element at index k is also less than or equal to that right child. If any such parent-child pair violates this ordering, the method returns false. The input array may be of any length, including zero (in which case the result is trivially true).
translated_ensures: result <==> forall k :: 0 <= k <= a.Length / 2 - 1 ==> (a[2*k+1] >= a[k] && (2*k+2 < a.Length ==> a[2*k+2] >= a[k]))

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_759
nl_requirement: The input s must be a string (no additional preconditions are required). The method returns true if and only if there exists at least one position in s where the character is a dot ('.') and there are exactly two characters after that dot (i.e., the dot appears at index |s| - 3), and returns false otherwise. In other words, result is true precisely when s contains a '.' such that the substring following it has length exactly 2.

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_760
nl_requirement: Given an integer array, the method returns true if and only if all elements in the array are equal to one another (i.e., every element equals the first element). If the array is empty, the method returns true. If the array contains at least one element that differs from the first element, the method returns false. There are no preconditions on the input beyond it being a valid integer array.
translated_ensures: result <==> forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> a[i] == a[0] || a.Length == 0

name: dafny-synthesis_task_id_769
nl_requirement: Given two sequences of integers a and b, the method returns a sequence diff containing exactly those integers that appear in a but do not appear in b, with no duplicates. Every element of diff must be present in a and absent from b, and every integer that appears in a and not in b must appear in diff. Additionally, all elements in diff are distinct — no integer appears more than once in the result. There are no preconditions on the inputs; both sequences may be empty or contain duplicates.
translated_ensures: forall x :: x in diff ==> x in a
forall x :: x in diff ==> x !in b
forall x :: (x in a && x !in b) ==> x in diff
